prompt: In the aggregate demand–aggregate supply (AD-AS) model, short-run equilibrium is defined as

options.label: A
options.text: the point at which aggregate demand equals zero and the price level is stable.

options.label: B
options.text: the point at which the SRAS curve intersects the LRAS curve.

options.label: C
options.text: the point at which the aggregate quantity of output demanded equals the aggregate quantity of output supplied — i.e., the intersection of the AD and SRAS curves.

options.label: D
options.text: the point at which real GDP equals potential GDP and unemployment equals the natural rate.

options.label: E
options.text: the point at which the price level equals 100 (the index base year).

explanation: Short-run equilibrium in the AD-AS model occurs where the AD curve and the SRAS curve intersect. At this point, the quantity of real GDP demanded by all sectors of the economy equals the quantity of real GDP supplied by all producers; this determines both the short-run equilibrium price level and the short-run equilibrium real GDP.

prompt: In the AD-AS model, long-run equilibrium is defined as

options.label: A
options.text: the intersection of the AD and SRAS curves at any price level.

options.label: B
options.text: the point where the price level stops changing over time.

options.label: C
options.text: the point at which the AD and SRAS curves intersect on the LRAS curve — at the full-employment level of real output (Yf).

options.label: D
options.text: the point where government spending equals tax revenue (balanced budget).

options.label: E
options.text: the intersection of the AD curve with the horizontal axis (zero price level).

explanation: Long-run equilibrium occurs when all three curves - AD, SRAS, and LRAS - intersect at the same point. This means: (1) the quantity demanded = quantity supplied (AD = SRAS), AND (2) the economy is at full-employment output (on the LRAS); at long-run equilibrium, there is no output gap, unemployment equals the natural rate, and there is no pressure for wages to change.

prompt: An economy is in long-run equilibrium when

options.label: A
options.text: the SRAS curve is to the left of the LRAS curve.

options.label: B
options.text: the AD curve intersects the LRAS curve at a price level above short-run equilibrium.

options.label: C
options.text: the AD and SRAS curves intersect ON the LRAS — real GDP equals full-employment output (Yf), unemployment equals the natural rate, and there is no output gap.

options.label: D
options.text: actual GDP exceeds potential GDP, creating an inflationary gap.

options.label: E
options.text: the price level is constant and real GDP is growing.

explanation: Long-run equilibrium requires all three curves to intersect at the same point. At this triple intersection on the LRAS: real GDP = Yf (full employment), unemployment = natural rate, no recessionary or inflationary output gap, and no sustained pressure for wages to rise or fall; this is the economy's long-run "anchor" position.

prompt: A "recessionary gap" (negative output gap) occurs when

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: the SRAS curve shifts to the right of the LRAS curve.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: real GDP exceeds potential GDP and unemployment falls below the natural rate.

options.label: E

The AD-SRAS intersection is to the LEFT of the LRAS; in this situation, the economy is underperforming: output is below capacity, unemployment exceeds the natural rate, and resources are underutilized.

prompt: An "inflationary gap" (positive output gap) occurs when

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: the LRAS curve shifts to the right of the SRAS curve.

options.label: C

options.label: D
options.text: actual GDP equals potential GDP and there is no output gap.

options.label: E

explanation: An inflationary gap (positive output gap) occurs when the short-run equilibrium real GDP > potential GDP (Yf). The AD-SRAS intersection is to the RIGHT of the LRAS; in this situation, the economy is overheating: output is above sustainable capacity, unemployment falls below the natural rate, and upward wage pressure builds.

prompt: On an AD-AS graph showing all three curves (AD, SRAS, LRAS), the short-run equilibrium is found at

options.label: A
options.text: the intersection of the SRAS and LRAS curves.

options.label: B
options.text: the intersection of the AD curve with the horizontal axis.

options.label: C

options.label: A
